title: Crèche Third Term
overview: Third-Term Curriculum Intent Third Term completes the child's Crèche curriculum journey. First Term established I AM SAFE -> I BELONG -> I EXPLORE. Second Term developed I PARTICIPATE -> I COMMUNICATE -> I MAKE CHOICES. Third Term develops I NOTICE -> I TRY -> I SOLVE -> I COMMUNICATE -> I DO MORE FOR MYSELF -> I AM READY TO MOVE FORWARD. The purpose is not to turn Third Term Crèche into Nursery, but to deepen security, communication, curiosity, physical capability and independence. Third-Term Progression Earlier Crèche Experience Third Term Progression Explore objects Explore with greater purpose Respond to words Understand and use increasing vocabulary Watch adults Participate and attempt Notice differences Begin comparing Move freely Move with increasing control Explore materials Select and use materials purposefully Play beside children Participate increasingly with others Receive help Attempt familiar routines Notice nature Observe simple change Hear stories Anticipate and participate Experience problems Try simple solutions Depend heavily on adults Seek appropriate help while attempting independently Annual Crèche progression: EXPERIENCE -> PARTICIPATE -> NOTICE -> TRY -> CONNECT Third-Term Curriculum Map Week Big Idea Main Development 1 I Am Growing Growth, change and identity 2 Plants Grow Too Growth, care and observation 3 Wonderful Water Sensory investigation and Practical Life 4 Water Around Us Uses of water, care and safety 5 Little Creatures Minibeasts, movement and observation 6 Consolidation / Calendar Flexibility Responsive review 7 Homes for Living Things Habitats, position and care 8 How Things Move and Work Cause, effect and problem-solving 9 I Can Make Things Happen Simple technology and purposeful action 10 Africa - Our Wider Home Identity and widening world knowledge 11 Sounds, Stories and Creativity Communication, imagination and expression 12 I Can Do More for Myself Independence and Nursery preparation 13 Moving Forward Reflection, celebration and transition Third-Term Communication Progression Adults continue expanding language naturally: 'You are pouring water into the cup'; 'A little ant is crawling'; 'The car is going down the ramp.' The objective is rich responsive interaction, not forced repetition. Third-Term Mathematics Spine Children encounter quantity, matching, sorting, comparison, big/small, more/less, full/empty, inside/outside, high/low, near/far, fast/slow, shape, space, pattern, capacity, simple sequencing and cause/effect. Progression: EXPERIENCE -> NOTICE -> COMPARE -> ANTICIPATE. Third-Term Literacy Entitlement Crèche literacy remains conversation, songs, rhymes, books, stories, sound play, environmental sounds, picture discussion, repeated refrains, meaningful names, drawing, scribbling, large-scale marks, fine-motor development and storytelling through play. There is no formal Reception SSP programme, spelling test, compulsory handwriting exercise or reading examination. Third-Term Continuous Provision Continue Books, Construction, Small World, Home/Role Play, Mathematics, Creative, Practical Life, Sensorial Experiences, Nature/Investigation and Outdoor Learning. Enhancements include plant/growth investigation, water exploration, minibeast observation, habitat small world, ramps, wheels, cause-effect resources, African stories/music and transition role play. Practical Life - End-of-Crèche Progression First Term: DO WITH ME -> Second Term: LET ME HELP -> Third Term: LET ME TRY -> Nursery: I CAN DO MORE. Children should enter Nursery not simply knowing more topics, but more capable. Outdoor Curriculum Provide plant observation, watering, weather, movement, large construction, water play, nature walks, small-creature observation, transport play, ramps, sound, shadow/light experiences and free physical exploration. Outdoor learning is curriculum, not merely break time. Christian Character Spine Third Term develops Gratitude, Patience, Stewardship, Gentleness, Care, Perseverance, Respect, Joy, Responsibility and Courage through everyday relationships and actions. Nigerian and African Knowledge By the end of Crèche, children should have meaningful encounters with identity, family, school, Owo/local community, Nigerian foods, markets, transport, weather, plants, animals, music, stories, clothing, Nigeria and introductory experiences of Africa. We build belonging before abstraction. Inclusion and SEND Transition must not be used to label children unfairly. Consider communication, home language, physical development, sensory processing, social interaction, emotional regulation, attention, hearing, vision, feeding, self-care, medical needs and strengths. Where concern exists: OBSERVE -> DISCUSS -> SUPPORT -> REVIEW -> REFER APPROPRIATELY. Parents remain partners. Parent Partnership Home connections may include baby photographs, plant watering, safe pouring, noticing rain and insects, building with boxes, pushing/rolling objects, Nigerian songs, African stories, handwashing, self-feeding, dressing participation, simple responsibilities and positive talk about Nursery. No Crèche homework packets are required. Crèche to Nursery Transition Profile Communication & Language: increasingly responds to familiar language, communicates needs, uses gestures/words/phrases according to development, attends to familiar stories and songs, and participates in interaction. PSED: forms secure relationships, participates in routines, shows preferences, plays alongside/with others, tolerates short waits with support and seeks help appropriately. Physical: moves confidently, manipulates objects, uses hands purposefully, participates in self-care and attempts simple dressing. Literacy foundations: enjoys and handles books, attends to stories, joins rhymes, notices sounds and makes marks. Mathematics foundations: meaningful experience of quantity, matching, sorting, size, position, pattern, shape, space, capacity and comparison. Understanding the World: notices people, places, nature, weather, plants, animals, materials, simple cause/effect and familiar cultural experiences. Expressive Arts: explores music, movement, drawing, paint, construction, pretend play and materials. Practical Life: increasingly carries, places, restores, pours, wipes, feeds, washes, helps, chooses and attempts. Transition question: IS THIS CHILD INCREASINGLY READY TO PARTICIPATE, COMMUNICATE, EXPLORE AND BECOME MORE INDEPENDENT IN NURSERY? Complete Crèche Annual Progression FIRST TERM - BELONG: I AM SAFE Security, relationships, routines, body awareness, family, senses, nature, early independence. SECOND TERM - PARTICIPATE: I TAKE PART Communication, choice, community, transport, food, building, culture, greater Practical Life participation. THIRD TERM - CONNECT: I EXPLORE WITH PURPOSE Growth, change, investigation, cause/effect, problem-solving, wider-world awareness, greater independence and transition. NURSERY: I AM READY TO EXPLORE, COMMUNICATE AND CONNECT MORE DEEPLY. Annual journey: BELONG -> PARTICIPATE -> CONNECT. End-of-Crèche Curriculum Entitlement Every child leaving AMES Crèche should have experienced secure relationships, rich conversation, stories, books, songs, rhymes, movement, outdoor learning, sensory exploration, early mathematics, nature, construction, creative expression, Practical Life, self-care, family and community knowledge, Nigerian identity, introductory African awareness, Christian character, choice, problem-solving and increasing independence. No child's Crèche experience should be judged primarily by worksheets completed. Teacher Year-End Review Teachers should be able to explain what the child enjoys; how the child communicates; which relationships support the child; what the child can now do independently; what the child understands; how the child approaches new experiences; emerging mathematical ideas; engagement with books and language; movement and manipulation; support still required; and what the Nursery teacher should know. This informs transition without becoming a bureaucratic checklist. Crèche Curriculum Quality Test Did children feel secure? Were relationships warm? Was language rich? Were books available every day? Did children sing, move, go outdoors, investigate, encounter mathematics meaningfully, experience nature, create and develop Practical Life? Did adults allow attempts? Did independence increase? Was Nigerian identity visible? Was Christian character lived? Were different developmental needs respected? Did assessment improve teaching? Did parents contribute? Was childhood protected? ARE OUR CHILDREN MORE CAPABLE THAN WHEN THEY ARRIVED? Crèche Third-Term & Year-End Declaration We welcomed children into security. We helped them belong, communicate, explore, participate and care. We gave real responsibilities and allowed attempts, mistakes and retrying. We filled their days with language, books, songs, movement, nature, mathematics, creativity and investigation. We strengthened independence, introduced community, celebrated Nigeria, began widening their world towards Africa and lived Christian character through everyday relationships. We prepare them for Nursery because they are increasingly secure, communicative, curious, capable, independent and ready to keep learning. HOW DOES THIS HELP THE CHILD FLOURISH? IN GOD WE TRUST. weeks.title: I Am Growing
weeks.curriculumIntent: Children notice that people grow and change.
weeks.sourceSection: Crèche Third Term / Week 1 - I Am Growing

items.title: Growth, change and identity
items.learningIntent: Children notice that people grow and change.
items.learningContent:
Children notice that people grow and change. Vocabulary: baby, child, grow, big, small, tall, old, new, me. Use books, personal
photographs where appropriate, movement and simple sequencing. Celebrate individual capability without comparing children.
Practical Life asks, 'What can I do now?' through carrying, feeding, wiping, restoring and dressing attempts. Character: Gratitude.
items.teachingGuidance:
Use books, personal
photographs where appropriate, movement and simple sequencing.
items.practicalLife: 'What can I do now?' through carrying, feeding, wiping, restoring and dressing attempts
items.sourceSection: Crèche Third Term / Week 1 - I Am Growing

weeks.title: Plants Grow Too
weeks.curriculumIntent: Revisit plants and deepen learning by noticing change over time: REVISIT -> DEEPEN -> APPLY.
weeks.sourceSection: Crèche Third Term / Week 2 - Plants Grow Too

items.title: Growth, care and observation
items.learningIntent: Revisit plants and deepen learning by noticing change over time: REVISIT -> DEEPEN -> APPLY.
items.learningContent:
Revisit plants and deepen learning by noticing change over time: REVISIT -> DEEPEN -> APPLY. Vocabulary: seed, plant, grow,
soil, water, leaf, flower, root. Plant a fast-growing seed where practical, observe regularly, water carefully and notice visible changes.
Explore small/bigger, one/more, full/empty and seed-to-plant sequence. Character: Stewardship and Patience.
items.assessmentFocus: Plant a fast-growing seed where practical, observe regularly, water carefully and notice visible changes.
items.sourceSection: Crèche Third Term / Week 2 - Plants Grow Too

weeks.title: Wonderful Water
weeks.curriculumIntent: Investigate water through first-hand sensory and mathematical experiences.
weeks.sourceSection: Crèche Third Term / Week 3 - Wonderful Water

items.title: Sensory investigation and Practical Life
items.learningIntent: Investigate water through first-hand sensory and mathematical experiences.
items.learningContent:
Investigate water through first-hand sensory and mathematical experiences. Vocabulary: water, wet, dry, pour, splash, full, empty,
float, sink. Explore pouring, scooping, squeezing, transferring, capacity and safe float/sink experiences without requiring formal
scientific explanations. Practical Life: pouring and wiping spills. Character: Care.
items.sourceSection: Crèche Third Term / Week 3 - Wonderful Water

weeks.title: Water Around Us
weeks.mainDevelopment: Uses of water, care and safety
weeks.curriculumIntent: Connect water with drinking, washing, cleaning, plant care, cooking through adult discussion and rain.
weeks.sourceSection: Crèche Third Term / Week 4 - Water Around Us

items.title: Uses of water, care and safety
items.learningIntent: Connect water with drinking, washing, cleaning, plant care, cooking through adult discussion and rain.
items.learningContent:
Connect water with drinking, washing, cleaning, plant care, cooking through adult discussion and rain. Vocabulary: drink, wash, bath,
rain, plant, clean, water, tap. Develop responsible habits and simple safety boundaries. Practical Life includes handwashing, plant
watering and cleaning. Character: Stewardship - we do not waste water.
items.teachingGuidance: Character: Stewardship - we do not waste water.
items.outdoorLearning: Connect water with drinking, washing, cleaning, plant care, cooking through adult discussion and rain.
items.practicalLife: Practical Life is included in the approved weekly guidance.
items.christianCharacter: Stewardship - we do not waste water
items.sourceSection: Crèche Third Term / Week 4 - Water Around Us

weeks.title: Little Creatures
weeks.curriculumIntent: Notice small living creatures safely and respectfully.
weeks.sourceSection: Crèche Third Term / Week 5 - Little Creatures

items.title: Minibeasts, movement and observation
items.learningIntent: Notice small living creatures safely and respectfully.
items.learningContent:
Notice small living creatures safely and respectfully. Vocabulary may include ant, butterfly, bee, snail, insect, small, crawl, fly, wing,
reflecting creatures children encounter. Observe movement, size, colour and location; use creature movement, matching, books,
songs and creative representation. Adults check outdoor areas and avoid unsafe handling. Character: Gentleness.
items.teachingGuidance:
Observe movement, size, colour and location; use creature movement, matching, books,
songs and creative representation.
items.outdoorLearning: Adults check outdoor areas and avoid unsafe handling.
items.assessmentFocus:
Observe movement, size, colour and location; use creature movement, matching, books,
songs and creative representation.

items.title: Responsive review
items.learningIntent: Responsive review rather than formal examination.
items.learningContent:
Responsive review rather than formal examination. Revisit growth, plants, water, small creatures, language, Practical Life,
movement, books, mathematics and social participation. Review observation length, vocabulary, problem-solving attempts,
independence, participation and routines, then strengthen needs before Nursery transition.

weeks.title: Homes for Living Things
weeks.curriculumIntent: Children notice that people and animals have places where they live.
weeks.sourceSection: Crèche Third Term / Week 7 - Homes for Living Things

items.title: Habitats, position and care
items.learningIntent: Children notice that people and animals have places where they live.
items.learningContent:
Children notice that people and animals have places where they live. Vocabulary: home, nest, tree, water, ground, inside, outside,
live. Use simple familiar associations without rigid inaccuracies. Explore inside/outside, on/under, high/low, matching, movement
trails, stories and building homes with blocks, boxes and natural materials. Character: Care.
items.teachingGuidance: Use simple familiar associations without rigid inaccuracies.

weeks.title: How Things Move and Work
weeks.sourceSection: Crèche Third Term / Week 8 - How Things Move and Work

items.title: Cause, effect and problem-solving
items.learningContent:
Investigate simple cause and effect. Vocabulary: push, pull, turn, roll, open, close, stop, go, work. Explore wheels, doors, lids, ramps,
safe cause-effect toys and switches. Adults ask 'What happened?' and model causal language. Use purposeful opening/closing,
turning and fitting. Character: Perseverance.

weeks.title: Africa: Our Wider Home
weeks.curriculumIntent: Widen the child's world from Nigeria towards Africa through positive encounter, not map memorisation.
weeks.sourceSection: Crèche Third Term / Week 10 - Africa: Our Wider Home

items.title: Identity and widening world knowledge
items.learningIntent: Widen the child's world from Nigeria towards Africa through positive encounter, not map memorisation.
items.learningContent:
Widen the child's world from Nigeria towards Africa through positive encounter, not map memorisation. Progression: Me -> Family ->
School -> Community -> Nigeria -> Africa. Experience varied African people, families, landscapes, homes, animals, music, art and
environments without presenting Africa as one culture. Reinforce 'We live in Nigeria' and 'Nigeria is in Africa' without testing.
Character: Respect and Love.
items.nigerianAfricanContext: Widen the child's world from Nigeria towards Africa through positive encounter, not map memorisation.
items.parentHomeConnection:

School -> Community -> Nigeria -> Africa.

weeks.title: Sounds, Stories and Creativity
weeks.curriculumIntent: Children increasingly use sound, movement, marks and materials to communicate ideas.
weeks.sourceSection: Crèche Third Term / Week 11 - Sounds, Stories and Creativity

items.title: Communication, imagination and expression
items.learningIntent: Children increasingly use sound, movement, marks and materials to communicate ideas.
items.learningContent:
Children increasingly use sound, movement, marks and materials to communicate ideas. Vocabulary: story, sing, sound, drum,
make, draw, dance, again. Use repeated stories, predictable refrains, rhymes, picture discussion, dance, rhythm, mark-making,
drumming, singing, painting, dough, construction and pretend play. Include Yoruba/Nigerian songs and stories alongside wider
literature. Character: Joy and Confidence.
items.teachingGuidance: Children increasingly use sound, movement, marks and materials to communicate ideas.
items.outdoorLearning:
Use repeated stories, predictable refrains, rhymes, picture discussion, dance, rhythm, mark-making,
drumming, singing, painting, dough, construction and pretend play.
items.nigerianAfricanContext:
Include Yoruba/Nigerian songs and stories alongside wider
literature.
items.sourceSection: Crèche Third Term / Week 11 - Sounds, Stories and Creativity

weeks.title: I Can Do More for Myself
weeks.bigIdea: I Can Do More for Myself
weeks.curriculumIntent: Consolidate independence for Nursery through capability rather than academic preparation.
weeks.sourceSection: Crèche Third Term / Week 12 - I Can Do More for Myself

items.title: Independence and Nursery preparation
items.learningIntent: Consolidate independence for Nursery through capability rather than academic preparation.
items.learningContent:
Consolidate independence for Nursery through capability rather than academic preparation. Children increasingly attempt to carry
belongings, find personal items, use cup/spoon, wash hands, wipe spills, restore resources, carry trays/baskets, dress simply, follow
routines, wait briefly, choose and ask for help. Core message: HELP ME TO DO MORE FOR MYSELF. Character: Responsibility
and Independence.
items.teachingGuidance: Consolidate independence for Nursery through capability rather than academic preparation.
items.montessoriPractice: Core message: HELP ME TO DO MORE FOR MYSELF.
items.sourceSection: Crèche Third Term / Week 12 - I Can Do More for Myself

weeks.title: Moving Forward
weeks.curriculumIntent: Celebrate the Crèche year and prepare emotionally for progression without formal graduation examination.
weeks.sourceSection: Crèche Third Term / Week 13 - Moving Forward

items.title: Reflection, celebration and transition
items.learningIntent: Celebrate the Crèche year and prepare emotionally for progression without formal graduation examination.
items.learningContent:
Celebrate the Crèche year and prepare emotionally for progression without formal graduation examination. Revisit favourite books,
songs, movement, Practical Life, plants, water, animals, construction, creativity and routines. Where appropriate, visit the Nursery
environment, meet adults, see familiar resources, share a story and return to the familiar Crèche base. Transition should be safe,
gradual, positive and predictable. Character: Courage and Gratitude.
items.teachingGuidance:
Where appropriate, visit the Nursery
environment, meet adults, see familiar resources, share a story and return to the familiar Crèche base.
